recurring.name: Iliad Intensive

recurring.name: Iliad Fellowship
recurring.description: Supports mentored research in applied mathematics for alignment, culminating in a research proposal. Aimed at PhD, postdoctoral, and similarly experienced researchers in math, physics, and related fields.

recurring.name: BlueDot Impact courses
recurring.description: Range from a short self-paced introduction to multi-week curricula on technical safety, AGI strategy, and frontier AI governance. Each week combines reading, writing, and a peer discussion meeting. Shorter intensive versions are also available.

recurring.name: Dovetail Research Fellowship
recurring.description: Mathematical AI safety research program with Dovetail, an agent foundations research group. Participants (must be UK-based) work solo or in small groups on pure-math problems – drawing on probability theory, information theory, and dynamical systems.

recurring.name: Anthropic Fellows Program
recurring.description: Provides funding, compute, and Anthropic mentorship for technical talent entering empirical AI safety research. Fellows work full-time on projects in scalable oversight, interpretability, and AI control, aiming to produce a paper. No PhD or prior ML experience required.
recurring.location: Online & Berkeley, USA & London, UK + more

recurring.name: MATS (Machine Alignment, Transparency, and Security)
recurring.description: Research program connecting researchers with top mentors in alignment, interpretability, governance, and security. Participants can also apply for a 6–12 month funded extension.

recurring.name: AFFINE Superintelligence Alignment Seminar
recurring.description: Helps newcomers acquire a deep understanding of the core problems of superintelligence alignment, explored from several perspectives. Includes workshops, lectures, debates, peer tutoring, and 1-1s with mentors.

recurring.name: AI Safety Camp (AISC)
recurring.description: Research program where participants form teams around preselected projects addressing AI risk. Research leads propose projects, then selected projects open for team member applications. Teams work together for about three months and present results at the end.

recurring.name: Human-Aligned AI Summer School
recurring.description: Intensive program covering current questions in technical alignment research and the broader framings that shape them – involving talks, workshops, expert panels, and discussions. Aimed at researchers, PhD students, and talented students familiar with alignment basics.

recurring.name: CLR Summer Research Fellowship
recurring.description: Program at the Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) exploring how to reduce suffering in the long-term future (s-risks) and related technical AI safety ideas. Participants join CLR's team for a supervised research project, with an emphasis on career development.

recurring.name: CHAI Internship
recurring.description: For students and professionals interested in research in human-compatible AI. Interns work on a research project supervised by – and often proposed by – a mentor at the Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI), which is typically then published as a first-author workshop paper.

recurring.name: Tarbell Fellowship
recurring.description: Program by the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism for journalists covering AI and people with AI expertise moving into journalism. Includes a course on AI and journalism fundamentals, a summit, and a newsroom placement.
recurring.location: Online & USA & UK & Hong Kong + more

recurring.name: Non-Trivial Fellowship
recurring.description: Helps people ages 14–20 launch research projects tackling the world's most pressing problems – including AI safety. Includes guided activities, facilitator mentorship, and scholarships and project grants for top scholars.

recurring.name: LawAI Research Fellowships
recurring.description: Run by the Institute for Law & AI (LawAI), these paid placements let law students, professionals, and academics work at the frontier of AI law and policy. Cohorts run each summer and winter across US Law, EU Law, and Legal Frontiers tracks. Includes mentorship and expert Q&As.
recurring.location: Online & Cambridge, UK & Washington D.C., USA

recurring.name: Effective Thesis Fellowship
recurring.description: Pairs students and early-career researchers with partner organizations working on global problems like AI safety. Participants develop a thesis or independent research project with mentorship, producing work that informs real-world decisions.

recurring.name: Apart Fellowship
recurring.description: Program from Apart Research that turns hackathon projects into peer-reviewed publications. Fellows work in small teams with structured mentorship, compute, and conference travel support. Entry is by performing well in one of Apart's sprints.

recurring.name: Frame Fellowship
recurring.description: Accelerator for content creators making video and social media content that educates the public about AI safety, with studio space and mentors. Two tracks: one for independent creators building their own channel, and one for those embedded with an organization to grow its reach.

recurring.name: SPAR (Supervised Program for Alignment Research)
recurring.description: Research program pairing mentees with experienced mentors on technical AI safety and governance projects, with compute and other project expenses funded. Each round ends in a virtual demo day.

recurring.name: ML4Good
recurring.description: Intensive training for people pursuing a career in AI safety, run in regional cohorts around the world. Offers a technical track and a governance and strategy track, both ending in a capstone project.

recurring.name: Foresight Fellowship
recurring.description: Helps early-career scientists, engineers, and innovators advance AI safety and other beneficial technologies. Participants join seminars, workshops, and conferences. Also includes connections to mentors, funders, and career counseling. No minimum time requirement.

recurring.name: Horizon Fellowship
recurring.description: Places AI and emerging technology experts in policy roles in Washington D.C. for up to two years. The Horizon Institute for Public Service provides policy training, mentorship, and matching with executive branch, congressional, and think tank hosts.

recurring.name: Astra Fellowship
recurring.description: Program hosted at Constellation's Berkeley research center, pairing emerging talent with senior advisors on alignment research, governance, and strategy projects. Fellows receive mentorship and career support.

recurring.name: Constellation Visiting Fellows
recurring.description: Lightly structured program for people working full-time on AI safety to continue their work from Constellation's research center in Berkeley. During that time fellows connect with leading researchers and find collaborators.

recurring.name: GovAI Fellowship
recurring.description: Governance program run by the Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI), aimed at early-career individuals and established professionals new to AI governance. Participants pursue a research or applied project under expert mentorship and build field connections.

recurring.name: Talos Fellowship
recurring.description: Launches and accelerates European AI policy careers focused on the safe and responsible deployment of advanced AI. Combines an 8-week online reading group with a week-long policymaking summit in Brussels, plus optional tracks including a paid placement.

recurring.name: ARENA (Alignment Research Engineer Accelerator)
recurring.description: Trains aspiring alignment researchers and engineers in ML through an intensive curriculum. Participants work through programming exercises in pairs under the guidance of expert teaching assistants.

recurring.name: Global Challenges Project (GCP)
recurring.description: Intensive residential workshop run by Kairos, exploring the foundational arguments around risks from advanced AI and biotechnology. Includes guest speakers, career planning, and 1-on-1s.

recurring.name: ERA:AI Fellowship
recurring.description: Research program for researchers and entrepreneurs mitigating risks from frontier AI. Fellows pursue a mentored project in technical AI safety, AI governance, or technical AI governance.

recurring.name: LASR Labs
recurring.description: Research program focused on reducing the risk of loss of control to advanced AI, tackling action-relevant questions on concrete threat models. Participants work in teams of 3–4 with an experienced supervisor to write an academic-style paper.

recurring.name: Pivotal AI Safety Fellowship
recurring.description: Program for projects spanning technical AI safety, governance, and AI-bio. Includes mentorship, research management, workshops, and workspace at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA). Provides continued funding of up to six months for strong work.

recurring.name: Pathfinder Fellowship
recurring.description: Supports students around the world who are organizing technical AI safety or AI policy university groups. Participants receive mentorship, funding, and other resources to develop into on-campus leaders, preparing themselves and their group members for careers in the field.

recurring.name: AI Governance Taskforce
recurring.description: Helps experienced professionals transition into AI governance careers. Small teams tackle policy-relevant research with expert partners like the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) and GovAI, typically producing a paper and a policy brief or article.

recurring.name: Algoverse AI Safety
recurring.description: Immerses participants in safety research through expert-led sessions and hands-on projects. Teams of three survey research agendas, build technical skills, and work with mentors to produce a paper for conference submission.

recurring.name: ARBOx (Alignment Research Bootcamp Oxford)
recurring.description: Intensive run by the Oxford AI Safety Initiative (OAISI) designed to rapidly build AI safety skills – covering interpretability, RLHF, and replicating alignment research papers. Expects basic familiarity with linear algebra, Python, and AI safety.

recurring.name: CAMBRIA
recurring.description: ML upskilling program from the Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI) for aspiring technical AI safety researchers. Covers mechanistic interpretability and reinforcement learning via the ARENA curriculum.

recurring.name: CBAI Research Fellowship
recurring.description: Research program run by the Cambridge Boston Alignment Initiative (CBAI). Fellows work closely with mentors on projects across interpretability, formal verification, and AI governance.

recurring.name: MARS (Mentorship for Alignment Research Students)
recurring.description: Research program from the Cambridge AI Safety Hub (CAISH), pairing teams of 2–4 with mentors on technical alignment and governance research. A one-week in-person kickoff leads into 8–10 weeks of remote work.

recurring.name: Cooperative AI Summer School
recurring.description: Intensive program for early-career professionals already working in or studying cooperative AI. Participants attend talks from researchers, work on collaborative projects tackling cooperative AI challenges, and receive career guidance and mentoring. Run by CAIF.

recurring.name: Introduction to Cooperative AI
recurring.description: Aims to deepen participants' understanding of the field of cooperative AI and help them prepare to contribute. Includes weekly exercises, group discussions facilitated by field practitioners, and a dedicated community. Run by Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF).

recurring.name: XLab Summer Research Fellowship
recurring.description: Run by UChicago's Existential Risk Laboratory (XLab), this program supports students and early-career researchers doing independent research on AI safety, AI security, or nuclear security. Includes expert mentorship.

recurring.name: Dilemmas and Dangers in AI
recurring.description: Run by Leaf for students aged 14–19 who haven't yet started university, exploring how to steer AI toward benefiting humanity. Includes discussion groups, talks and Q&As with AI safety researchers, and mentorship.

recurring.name: Future Impact Group (FIG) Fellowship
recurring.description: Participants work as research associates on projects supervised by experienced leads. Topics span AI policy, technical safety, and AI sentience. Provides research experience and helps build professional networks.

recurring.name: HIP Impact Accelerator Program (IAP)
recurring.description: Program run by High Impact Professionals (HIP) helping experienced mid-career and senior professionals transition into high-impact careers – including AI safety. Participants follow a guided workbook, attend weekly group sessions, and receive continued support after the program.

recurring.name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
recurring.description: Strengthens practical policy skills for a world with powerful AI. Professionals from varied backgrounds pursue independent projects with expert mentorship, joining in Washington D.C. or remotely after an in-person residency.
recurring.location: Online & Washington D.C., USA & London, UK

recurring.name: Athena Mentorship Program
recurring.description: Program for women strengthening their research skills and network in technical and policy-focused AI safety research. Participants join weekly research talks and gather midway for a retreat with established researchers.

recurring.name: ILINA Junior Research Fellowship
recurring.description: Program by ILINA, an African-led AI safety organization, helping participants develop high-impact projects and build career capital. Weekly seminars lead into mentored research on technical or governance tracks.

recurring.name: BASE Fellowship
recurring.description: Program by Black in AI Safety and Ethics (BASE) developing Black researchers in AI safety and security. Fellows work on a focused project with a mentor across alignment, security, governance, and responsible AI tracks.

recurring.name: Meridian Visiting Researcher Programme
recurring.description: Residency for AI safety researchers, providing workspace, community, research management, and support toward publication. Ideal for MATS-like program graduates transitioning to independent research, or experienced researchers seeking collaborators.

recurring.name: Orion AI Policy Accelerator
recurring.description: Program run by Arcadia Impact to help participants launch a career in AI policy. Five weeks of training on AI capabilities, risks, and policy levers lead into a supervised team research project.

recurring.name: Paragon Policy Fellowship
recurring.description: Hands-on, project-based program connecting students and recent graduates with US state and local governments to research and write policy briefs on emerging tech issues, including AI governance. Work is done in small teams.

recurring.name: RAND CAST Fellowship
recurring.description: Currently paused. Develops policy analysts at the intersection of AI and security through mentored research on frontier AI security, compute governance, and technology policy. Part-time is also possible.

recurring.name: TARA (Technical Alignment Research Accelerator)
recurring.description: Program based on the ARENA curriculum, building technical AI safety skills across the Asia-Pacific region. Saturday sessions in cities across Australia, New Zealand, and Asia cover transformers, interpretability, RL, and evaluations, then a research project.

recurring.name: AI Security Bootcamp (AISB)
recurring.description: Equips experienced security professionals to secure frontier AI systems. Covers adversarial ML, LLM security, and AI infrastructure through demos and hands-on red/blue team exercises.

recurring.name: Lens Academy courses
recurring.description: Cohort-based courses on superintelligence risk. Each week combines readings, exercises with an AI tutor, and a guided group discussion. Also runs intensive versions. Anyone can join, with no selection process.

recurring.name: PIBBSS Fellowship
recurring.description: Interdisciplinary research program connecting PhD and postdoctoral researchers from fields like mathematics, neuroscience, physics, and philosophy with AI safety mentors. Projects bridge the participant's field and AI safety.
